description: From a cold boot to the party-selection screen of a NEW single-player run. Every step below was executed successfully against the live game on 2026-08-23; anything unproven is marked.
produces: A new Age of Rebellion run, Apprentice difficulty, sitting at party selection with four empty slots.
safety: NEVER click 'continue-btn' or 'load-btn'. Those resume the owner's live co-op campaign.
The selector 'Continue' is ambiguous: it substring-matches BOTH the safe 'next-btn' and the dangerous 'continue-btn'. Always select by the full button name or by a text that is unique on screen.
notes: The game boots into MULTIPLAYER_LOBBY and fails to rejoin a stale online adventure, leaving a modal. Steps 1-2 escape it. This is the game's own behaviour, not the harness's.
Difficulty MUST be lowered off Master: the footer warns 'Manual Saves will not be available on Master Difficulty', which would silently disable saveUser and make fixture capture impossible.
route is NOT a reliable signal here - it reported MAIN_MENU while the multiplayer browser was still on screen. Verify position with crucible_ui_dump instead.
Difficulty is STICKY between sessions. It was still APPRENTICE on the second run, so a script must READ difficulty-inp and only step it if needed, never assume it starts at Master.
Selector ambiguity: 'next-btn' substring-matches 'party-container-next-btn'. Prefer gamepad presses (rb/lb) or fully unambiguous names over selectors on this screen.

CONFIRMED: the party screen selects OUR ClassForge classes. class-text-selector reads CF_EOR_THIEF / CF_EOR_TRICKSHOT - the pack is live in character creation, and a class can be chosen by its exact id rather than by display name.
Focus is lost between steps. A gamepad press only acts on a focused target, so re-establish focus (ui_click or ui_focus) before each pad press rather than assuming it persisted.
The boot auto-join is a RACE: the game reached MAIN_MENU and then routed itself to MULTIPLAYER_LOBBY about two seconds later. Let the boot settle before navigating, and re-check where you are.

steps.why: select the focused adventure (The Resistance). Submit rather than a selector: all nine art holders share one name.
steps.expect: adventure-name-text and a difficulty selector on screen

steps.why: the difficulty control is a TextSelector, not a button; it responds to navigation, not clicks
step down again (JOURNEYMAN -> APPRENTICE), which restores manual saves
focus a slot. The gamepad press in step 11 needs a focus target - pressing A with nothing focused does nothing.
fill the focused slot. Synthetic UI events do NOT work here; the game reads its own input action. This also switches the game to controller prompts.
steps.expect: add-character-btn count drops by one; a class selector appears

steps.why: the class control is a TextSelector like difficulty - it navigates, it does not click. Its text is the CLASSFORGE ID, e.g. CF_EOR_THIEF, not the display name.
cycle the class. Read the selector's text after each step and stop when it equals the wanted id. Proven: CF_EOR_THIEF -> CF_EOR_TRICKSHOT. 'left' cycles back.
steps.expect: class-text-selector text becomes the next CF_EOR_* id

steps.why: repeat 10-13 for each of the four slots
steps.status: UNPROVEN - four-slot loop not yet run end to end

completion_signal.rule: enabled becomes True once four characters are chosen
completion_signal.why: the screen shows 'Party Not Ready' until then, and the button's enabled flag is readable in a dump - a clean machine-checkable gate

open: The four-slot loop has not been run end to end.
The full ordered class list is unmapped - cycle and record class-text-selector text to build it.
saveUser has not been proven to round-trip a position.
crucible_ui_dump intermittently exceeds the 10s main-thread budget on heavy screens; it walks ~24k elements.
